q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of an LED street light?
title: LED street light carbon footprint per unit
short: Weigh the die-cast aluminium housing and add the LED board, driver, lens and cable per fitting with supplier figures. Add assembly and burn-in testing electricity, then divide the unit's energy by fittings passed, stated by wattage.
audience: LED street light makers and municipal buyers

ul: Die-cast aluminium housing and heat sink.
Lens or glass cover, gaskets and cable.
Die casting and powder coating if done in-house.

p: Report per fitting by wattage. The aluminium housing is often the heaviest part, so its source matters.

example.title: Worked example: LED street light unit per unit (one month)
lines: Plant total: 25,400 / 6,000 = 4.233 kg CO2 per unit
Add housing, LED board and driver for the full figure
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use your own bills and production records.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh for FY 2024-25, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
